subject.title: feat(slack): support running as a real Slack user (user identity)

question: Should OpenClaw ship an opt-in bundled Slack mode that acts with a human user OAuth identity and receives that user’s DM/group-DM events through a companion app?
rationale: This is a new account-level configuration and credential-authority mode, not a repair of an established behavior; tests cannot decide the repository’s acceptable Slack-policy, user-consent, and support boundary.

options.title: Sponsor with live proof
options.body: Keep the direction, but require redacted real-workspace proof of DM/MPIM event delivery, self suppression, and outbound replies before merge.

options.title: Keep bot-only Slack
options.body: Decline the bundled personal user-OAuth mode and retain the existing bot identity as the supported Slack boundary.

options.title: Move to an extension path
options.body: If maintainers want to avoid expanding the bundled channel’s credential boundary, pursue the capability through an external plugin after confirming the required event and setup APIs are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Sponsor with live proof
recommendation.body: Keep the direction, but require redacted real-workspace proof of DM/MPIM event delivery, self suppression, and outbound replies before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the end-to-end feature series and are assigned on the PR, making them the best available routing candidate for the implementation and its supporting Slack evidence.
